headline_seed: Panama rocked by 2 powerful earthquakes and multiple aftershocks, prompting evacuations - AP News

consensus_facts: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck Panama on Friday, October 9, 2026, according to the US Geological Survey.
The earthquake was centered about 6 miles (10km) southwest of the remote community of Pitaloza Arriba, roughly 100+ miles southwest of Panama City.
The quake triggered tsunami warnings for multiple countries in Central and South America, including Colombia, Ecuador, Nicaragua, and Guatemala.
Tremors were felt in Panama City, where buildings shook and people evacuated into the streets.
The earthquake was followed by powerful aftershocks.
President José Raúl Mulino called for calm and said no deaths had been reported immediately after the quake.

framing_analysis.Bloomberg: Frames the event in economic and historical terms — leads with 'strongest earthquake in more than seven decades' and foregrounds the USGS estimate of $1 billion-plus in regional economic losses. Emphasizes no immediate deaths and the quake's distance from the Panama Canal (an implicit business/markets angle). Most of the retrievable text is site chrome; usable reporting is thin.
framing_analysis.The New York Times: Appears twice in the dossier. Article 2 is a Google News aggregation cluster listing many outlets' headlines rather than NYT body text; Article 7 is headline-only ('Map: Large Earthquake Shakes Panama'), signaling an explainer/visual-forward approach. No substantive NYT body text is available to analyze.
framing_analysis.Al Jazeera English: Leads with the tsunami-warning dimension and regional scope, naming affected countries. Provides on-the-ground color (eyewitness Rosendo Dominguez via AP, collapsed historic tower in Penonome) and contextualizes with other 2026 regional quakes (Venezuela twin quakes killing ~6,500 in June; Colombia's 7.4 killing ~289 in August). Frames Panama within a pattern of regional seismic disaster.
framing_analysis.Axios: Classic Axios 'big picture / driving the news / between the lines' breakdown. Emphasizes scale via USGS data (4.6 million people felt moderate-to-severe shaking, 'disaster likely widespread') while reassuring on the Panama Canal angle. Flags it as a breaking, to-be-updated story. Much of the retrievable text is cookie-consent boilerplate.
framing_analysis.NBC News: Provides the most granular seismological detail: a 7.7 initial quake, a 6.6 follow-on roughly three hours later, aftershocks between 4.8 and 5.8, and 45+ aftershocks per University of Panama seismologists. Also the broadest tsunami-warning country list. Credits The Associated Press as co-byline. Leads on the sequence/scale of the seismic event itself.
framing_analysis.CNN: Human-interest/eyewitness framing built around a video package: photojournalist Carlos Martinelli describing his car swaying and people fleeing buildings. Captions describe a '7.6 magnitude' quake and state no casualties or damage reported so far. Reporting is minimal text; the story is the firsthand account and footage.

primary_source_alignment: No primary sources (USGS bulletins, Panamanian government statements, tsunami center advisories) were included in the dossier, so no direct report-versus-document comparison is possible.
Multiple outlets attribute core facts to the USGS and the US Tsunami Center, but the underlying advisories themselves were not provided for verification.
missing_context: No outlet in the dossier provides a confirmed casualty or injury count beyond 'no deaths reported immediately' — the human toll remains unresolved at the time of coverage.
The magnitude figure is inconsistent across outlets (7.7 vs. 7.6 appearing in CNN and NBC captions); no source reconciles whether this reflects a revised USGS estimate or caption error.

Whether there were one or two distinct major quakes is unsettled — only NBC clearly describes a separate 6.6 event three hours later, while Bloomberg/Axios/Al Jazeera frame it as one quake plus aftershocks.
No primary USGS bulletin, Panamanian civil-protection statement, or official tsunami advisory was included in the dossier for verification.
No outlet details whether tsunami warnings were later downgraded, cancelled, or whether any actual waves were observed.
Depth of the quake (6 miles, per NBC) is reported by only one outlet and not corroborated.
The $1 billion economic-loss figure (Bloomberg) is a single-outlet, early USGS modeled estimate and is not independently corroborated in the dossier.

Articles 1 (Bloomberg), 4 (Axios), 5 (NBC), and 6 (CNN) contained large volumes of website navigation, cookie-consent, and subscription boilerplate rather than article text, limiting the retrievable reporting; Article 2 is a Google News headline cluster, not NYT body text.
brief.suggested_post_type_reason: Five outlets with usable body text reported the same event but with materially divergent framings (economic vs. tsunami-scope vs. seismological-detail vs. eyewitness) and unreconciled facts — notably magnitude (7.7 vs. 7.6) and whether there were one or two major quakes — making this a coverage-comparison story rather than a straightforward REPORT.
